newsitem.title: UK: Poor resettlement cost Montserrat lives - British MP.
newsitem.headline: Poor resettlement cost Montserrat lives - British MP.

text.p: A British member of parliament on Monday blamed many of the deaths caused by a volcanic eruption on the Caribbean island of Montserrat last week on poor resettlement efforts after a previous eruption.

Labour legislator Diane Abbott told parliament that small farmers who left the volcano area two years ago after an earlier eruption had come back to their land in the danger zone "because that was the only way they felt they could survive".
"Had there been proper housing, had there been proper arrangements made for their resettlement, they would not have lost their lives," Abbott said.
Nine people died and a further 10 are missing, presumed dead, following the new volcanic eruption on the British colony.
Abbott, who met leaders of Montserrat expatriate organisations in London last week, had successfully demanded a government statement on the position in the island.
Junior international development minister George Foulkes did not directly comment on Abbott's claims.
But he implicitly criticised the previous British Conservative government for its administration of the island.
"In the past there has been a lack of concern for the long-term interests of the people of Montserrat," he said.
Foulkes said the new government would do all it could to keep Montserrat a sustainable community.
"Assuming that there is not any further serious eruption, we would want to keep Montserrat as a viable entity," he said.
"That is why we are encouraging people to stay there. We will give them as much assistance as we can to stay there."
The population of Montserrat, a tourist and rice-growing economy in the eastern Caribbean close to Antigua, has fallen to about 6,800 from 11,000 when the volcano first became active.
Britain brought in emergency help after the latest eruption, mobilising four military helicopters and sending aid worth 6.8 million pounds ($11.3 million).
Junior foreign office minister Baroness Symons was due to return to London on Tuesday from a visit to the island to assess the situation. ($1=.6006 Pound)
